title: Session pacing surge: customer slowdown investigation and emergency rollback plan
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several enterprise customers reported abrupt throughput collapses and large first-token latency regressions starting 2026-03-01 02:20 UTC. Affected deployments include Hosted (us-west1) and a small set of Private clusters running the v2 runtime and adaptive session pacing enabled by default. Symptoms: TTFT for affected calls rose from ~120ms to 600-900ms; sustained tokens/sec fell from ~180-220 to ~40-80 for active sessions; error rate remained low but responses were extremely delayed. Customers reported timeouts at the application level (30s). Initial scope includes 3 paying customers (Acme Analytics, BetaDocs Inc, and a healthcare pilot) with multiple production endpoints. Immediate action is to diagnose root cause, restore normal latency for customers, and perform a controlled rollback or patch with telemetry-driven verification.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use hosted API in us-west1 with model llama2-13b-int8 variant and long priming (context ~8k tokens). 2) Send steady stream of user messages with bursts (10 requests concurrently, repeated patterns). 3) Observe scheduler Q depth and per-session pacing tokens_budget; note TTFT and tokens/sec via /metrics endpoints and console. 4) Reproduce on a Private cluster vpc-123 with same model and session traffic pattern. (Test harness scripts: https://git.internal/redwood/tests/session_pacing_surge.sh)
observed_metrics:
- TTFT (first-token latency) increased from median 120ms to median 650ms for affected sessions in us-west1.
- Tokens/sec per session dropped from median 200 -> 55.
- Scheduler queue length increased by 3-4x for sessions with long priming.
- EWMA of inter-arrival rate drifted upward causing per-session pacing budget to be set to near-zero for new microbatches.
- No CPU/GPU saturation; GPU utilization steady at 35-55%.
initial_hypothesis: A change in the adaptive session-pacing heuristic (commit 9f2b7c in runtime-2.3.0) incorrectly computes the expected token arrival rate for long-primed sessions. The heuristic clamps budgets aggressively when observed inter-arrival variance exceeds the threshold; a bug in the variance calc produced spurious large variance values for sessions with long prompt tokens, throttling their microbatch emission and starving tokens/sec despite spare GPU capacity.
mitigation_plan: 1) Emergency rollback option: flip feature flag 'adaptive_pacing_v2' -> false for hosted region us-west1 and push a rolling restart to Private clusters (target customers first). 2) If rollback is slow, apply a hot patch to scheduler to temporarily relax clamp thresholds (PR linked below) and trigger a controlled drain of suspect sessions. 3) Add short-term rate-limiter on session admission to prevent new long-primed sessions from starting until pacing is stabilized. 4) Notify affected customers with estimated 30-90min recovery window.
runbook_actions_taken:
- 2026-03-01 03:05 UTC: Pager duty triage (lead: Maya Chen).
- 2026-03-01 03:18 UTC: Disabled adaptive_pacing_v2 in us-west1 via feature-flag (Luis Ortega).
- 2026-03-01 03:25 UTC: Observed partial recovery for hosted customers (TTFT dropping to ~220ms).
- 2026-03-01 04:10 UTC: Pushed feature-flag toggle to Private customer vpc-123 (operator-assisted).
- 2026-03-01 04:35 UTC: Confirmed customer-side application timeouts subsided.
- 2026-03-01 05:00 UTC: Opened rollback PR to revert commit 9f2b7c for full release-channel rollback (PR #4521).
code_changes:
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/4521 - Revert adaptive pacing heuristic changes.
Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/4523 - Temporary relax clamp and add EWMA smoothing to variance calculation.
Note: patch includes unit tests for variance calc and an integration test harness that simulates long-primed sessions.
deployment_strategy: Canary rollout: 5% of capacity for 30m -> evaluate TTFT/tokens/sec -> 25% for 30m -> 100% if stable. Prioritize customer clusters: (1) Acme Analytics (hosted), (2) BetaDocs private vpc-123, (3) healthcare pilot (staged). Notify SRE and Account teams at each step.
